subject: docs/implementation/m3/snapshot-plan-c/PROPOSAL.md

requestedDecisions.claim: Row 8 changes component-closure admission into selection from J1 r4's already-admitted manifest set, using R10a on the durable path and ER10a on the ephemeral path. It adds no second admission or post-draw manifest refusal. The component admission path of item 7 must have run no later than that pre-draw boundary. This implements M3-D r3 item 24, SD-6 and F11.

M3-D item 24 concerns manifest-class refusals and defines its admitted population as component manifests. Its 'only among manifests' and forbidden-substitute wording must be read within that population. Authenticated core-inventory role projections are not such manifests. R7 correctly preserves row 8's core evaluator and detector selections. Item 9 is byte-unchanged, so the core provider's import and syntax-universe uses, its conditional direct Plan membership, and the adapter's import-only restriction also remain intact. This agrees with accepted J1 r4 S19's explicit preservation of all core role closures; it does not permit a new manifest admission at row 8.

The new sentence scopes item 7's closure-retention obligation to the closures row 8 selects, expressly the population r6's row 8 admitted. It neither removes retention of a selected closure's manifest body/whole tree nor makes every R10a-admitted selectable manifest an input of this Run. Without this clarification, moving manifest admission earlier could invite an incorrect expansion of 'every admitted closure' to the larger pre-selection population. Item 7 itself is byte-unchanged; the sentence is a lawful clarification of SD-6's admission-to-selection move.

The row now consumes both step 7's prechecked selection and the earlier host's admitted manifest set. Durable order is R10 trust view, R10a component admission, R11 handoff, R12 analysis-attempt draw, then capture/discovery/precheck/row-8 selection. On the ephemeral path ER10a precedes the attempt's draw and fence release/capture. A refusal therefore stays before the analysis-attempt reservation; the first-use creation prelude's distinct reservation remains the accepted exception. R10, R11 and R12 themselves are unchanged from accepted J1 r3, and no other M3-C order row changes.

The four diff hunks contain six change blocks: title, draft label, r6 acceptance/r7 summary, r7 changes table, SD-6 row 8, and the expressly permitted R1 update for C6-NB-01. Reversing those exact blocks restores r6 byte for byte. Item 7, item 9, all other numbered order rows, acceptance gate and unit section are unchanged. R5 and r6 row 8 are identical, so M3-D's r5 citation addresses the reviewed baseline. R1 now correctly records the two already-admitted core-provider uses and membership condition.
